brief: October core CPI delivered a third straight upside surprise, printing exactly the 0.30% m/m threshold Governor Waller had flagged as grounds to consider a 50bp December hike instead of 25bp. JPM still expects the FOMC goes 25bp, though market-implied pricing moved up (December meeting +27bp cumulative). The three-month core CPI pace hit 3.7%, the fastest since early 2025/late 2024, while core PPI missed JPM's forecast by a tenth even as upstream intermediate-goods pressure keeps building. The Fed also reshuffled its 2027 calendar: an October meeting becomes a policy-free 'Strategy Meeting,' the December 2027 meeting shifts to mid-November, and the calendar no longer flags which meetings carry a Summary of Economic Projections, leaving its fate unclear. Housing keeps weakening under higher mortgage rates: existing home sales hit their lowest level since 2010, NAHB sentiment sits near a 14-year low, and pending sales matched a record low dating to the series' 1999 start. Brent eased to $96 this week but JPM still forecasts $71 by 1Q27. Globally, JPM's two-pillar view (resilient growth, sticky inflation) argues markets and central banks are near the end of 'magical thinking,' with the BoE, BoJ, India and Thailand all leaning toward more hikes even as lower oil lets some EM central banks ease.
